hypothesis: States anywhere in binary64 are classified with the code unchanged through PLSR's power-of-two state scaling (components more than about 2^1022 below the largest one become subnormal in the scaled state and vanish beyond about 2^1075, which a code decided relative to |x|^2 does not see); the reported unscaled V and x^T M x equal the exact values to within rounding or are flagged value_out_of_range, and the flag is set exactly when the exact value is not representable; matrices whose arithmetic leaves binary64 return NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW or an input refusal; no level-set exceedance is missed near the limits. The resolution floor of a subnormal plant is T101's finding, which T103 cites and does not repeat.
input_data: A = [[-1, 2], [0, -3]], P = I with ten states from 2^-1074 to 1.797e308 (mixed scales included) and non-finite states
The same plant at 27 single-component states m 2^e (m in {1, 1.5, 1.9}, e in {-540..-536, -530, 510, 511, 512}) where s^2 underflows or overflows
Near-limit matrices: A = -2^1000 I with P = 2^30 I; A = -2^511 I or -2^512 I with P = 2^511 I; P = 2^1022 I with x = (1.5, 1.5); affine A(theta) = -I + theta c I, theta = +-1e308
The subnormal witness A = [[-2, 5], [0, -3]] 2^-1074, P = I (re-evaluated for the artifact only; its finding is retained by T101)
mathematical_model: V(x) = x^T P x and x^T M x are homogeneous of degree two in x, so PLSR evaluates at x / 2^e with the unit state in [1, 2), and reports V = s^2 * scaled_value (s = 2^e), flagging value_out_of_range when that product is infinite or zero while scaled_value is not. The level gate decides V > level as scaled_value > level / s^2 and treats an infinite s^2 as 'exceeded' and a zero s^2 as 'not exceeded'. Exact truth: V = 2^(p + 2e) for P = 2^p I and x = 2^e e1; V and x^T M x of every declared state in rationals.
numerical_result: 10 states from 2^-1074 to 1.797e308: 0 code changes (all CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN). Reported values at 37 states: 20 exact V or x^T M x not representable, 0 of them without value_out_of_range; 2 representable subnormal values flagged and reported as 0 (s^2 underflowed); unflagged values within 0.5 roundings of the exact ones. Level scan (68 cases): 5 missed exceedances (certified with V > level, s^2 underflowed), 9 spurious exceedances (s^2 overflowed), 0 disagreements with the documented rule. Near-limit matrices: {'A=-2^1000 I, P=2^30 I': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'A=-2^511 I, P=2^511 I': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', 'A=-2^512 I, P=2^511 I': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'P=2^1022 I, x=(1.5, 1.5)': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW'}. theta overflow: {'theta:+1e308,c=1': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'theta:-1e308,c=1': 'NUMERICAL_OVERFLOW', 'theta:+1e308,c=2': 'raises ValueError'}. Subnormal witness, re-evaluated for the artifact only (T101 retains its finding 'PLSR's resolution of a subnormal plant is zero while forming its decrease matrix rounds an exactly indefinite declared form to a negative definite one'): resolution 0, formed decrease matrix off the exact form by 1 x 2^-1074 in its largest entry (its code is retained in the artifact). Conclusion: state scaling and matrix overflow behave as documented; the hypothesis is refuted by level-gate errors (missed, spurious), by an input error raised for an in-box theta, by value_out_of_range set for representable subnormal values.
observation_model: PLSR code (or raised input error) per case; PLSR's reported V, x^T M x and value_out_of_range against exact rationals; exact exponent arithmetic for V against the level; PLSR's formed decrease matrix and resolution of the witness against its exact rational form.

title: Test overflow and underflow state evaluation.
uncertainty: The level scan, the reported-value states and the overflow cases involve exact powers of two or single-component states, so they are platform-independent; the witness's formed matrix and zero resolution are IEEE-deterministic, while its code depends on LAPACK's subnormal handling and is retained in the artifact only.
unresolved_assumptions: Near-limit inputs are synthetic binary64 numbers chosen to reach the limits, not plant data.
The documented level rule is transcribed from the runtime source at the pinned commit, so agreement with it is a same-specification check; the exact exponent comparison is the independent reference.
Mixed-scale states lose their smallest components in the scaled evaluation; with a strictly negative definite test form this cannot change the code and is not probed further here.
